I’ve been feeling really off for the past year—mostly just sad, like I can’t shake this weight no matter what. I used to love going out with friends, but now I cancel plans last minute, not because I don’t care, but I just don’t have the energy. Some days, getting out of bed feels impossible, even after sleeping 10 hours. Last winter, I thought I couldn’t keep going—I even saved up pills, though I didn’t go through with it. My husband noticed… we’ve been growing distant.

But then, about a month ago, things shifted. I didn’t feel tired anymore. I’d stay up until 4 a.m., not because I couldn’t sleep, but because I felt so *alive*—like my brain was buzzing. I started sketching wild design ideas, texting friends nonstop, talking so fast they’d ask me to slow down. I went shopping, bought clothes I didn’t need. I felt… desirable, for the first time in ages. I was initiating sex constantly—my husband was happy, but I could tell he was also a little overwhelmed.

Now the energy’s fading. I’m crashing again. The thing is, I don’t know if this is all part of depression… or something else. I’ve always been energetic, but I can’t remember if it’s always been *this* intense.
D009-D003_h001.question_a:

I used to love collaborating with my design teams, but lately, I’ve been pulling away, not answering messages, skipping meetings. It got so bad I even wrote a note to my husband, just in case… I couldn’t keep living like that.

Before this past year, though—last spring—I was the opposite. I felt amazing. I was dating like crazy, not just happy but *on fire*—had this buzzing energy, couldn't sit still, like my brain was sprinting. I’d stay up all night redesigning personal projects, talking fast, barely letting anyone get a word in. I remember my husband saying, “You’re not you,” but I felt so sharp, so alive.

But here’s the thing—that intense energy, the sleeplessness, the rapid talking—it only happened during those few weeks. It didn’t start in childhood. I wasn’t like that in school or college. This was new. It only flared up *then*. The rest of the time—especially now—it’s just this deep, heavy sadness I can’t shake.
D009-D003_h001.question_b:

My husband tells me I talk a mile a minute, especially when I’m excited, and that I don’t seem to need sleep sometimes—we’ve gone nights where I’m up till 3 a.m. just wired, planning or researching random things.

About a year ago, after a project failed and I felt overwhelmed, everything crashed. I withdrew from friends, stopped caring about work, felt constantly exhausted no matter how much I slept. But here’s the thing: the restlessness, the fast speech, the hyper focus on projects or sex drive spikes—they’re not new or episodic. They’ve been with me since childhood. It’s not that I have bursts of energy followed by crashes. It’s that the *baseline* of my mind has always been racing.

My wife says I’ve pulled away. I’ve had thoughts that life isn’t worth it, though I’m not planning anything. But then, out of nowhere, there were times—about a month ago—when things flipped. I’ve been married for over forty years, and my wife says I’ve never been like this before—she’s worried, and honestly, so am I. About a year ago, things started going downhill. I just felt… empty. I couldn’t enjoy my grandson’s visits, didn’t care about gardening, which I used to love. Most days, I’d lie in bed, drained, even after sleeping all night. I caught myself thinking, *Would it really matter if I weren’t here?* Not planning anything, mind you—just wondering.

But then, around two months ago, something shifted. I suddenly had all this energy—I cleaned the garage, started fixing the roof, even called old colleagues about starting a consulting business. I’d talk fast, I know—my wife says she can’t get a word in. I felt great, sharp, even flirted with her like we were newlyweds. I didn’t *need* sleep—four hours felt like enough, and I was up pacing, writing ideas. But those burst of energy? They weren’t lifelong. I wasn’t like this as a kid, or working years. Just recently—only during these high spells.
D009-D003_h004.question_b:
I’ve always been this way—my wife says I’ve never sat still a day in my life. Even as a kid, I was the one teachers complained about: too loud, couldn’t wait my turn, always blurting out answers. I’d start projects—woodworking, gardening, fixing the car—but rarely finish. That’s just how my mind works. Now at 68, it hasn’t changed. For the past month, I’ve felt that familiar buzz: talking fast, jumping from one idea to another, full of energy. My wife says I’m impossible to interrupt, like my mouth can’t keep up with my thoughts. I’m up late tinkering in the garage, not feeling tired. And honestly, the old spark’s back—feeling frisky, which surprises both of us.

But that’s only part of it. For about the last year, I’ve felt… hollow. I don’t enjoy the little things anymore—my morning coffee, the birds outside, nothing. I’m exhausted all the time, even after sleeping. I catch myself thinking, “Would it be easier just not to wake up?” I’ve never made plans, but the thought won’t leave.

The doctors talk about mood swings, but this hyper stuff? It’s not new. It’s been with me since I was a boy—long before these low spells ever started.
